basic_information.name: Lovable (formerly GPT Engineer)
basic_information.creator: Lovable Labs Inc., founded by Anton Osika (CEO) and Fabian Hedin (CTO) in Stockholm, Sweden (November 2023). Both are KTH graduates; Osika previously worked at CERN and co-founded Depict.ai.
basic_information.description: Lovable is an AI-powered full-stack web application builder that lets non-technical users describe a business idea in plain English and generates a complete, deployable React application with backend integration. Born from the viral open-source GPT Engineer project (52,000 GitHub stars), it rebranded to Lovable in late 2024 and became the fastest-growing European startup in history, reaching $100M ARR in 8 months. For entrepreneurs, Lovable dramatically reduces the gap between idea and working MVP: a functional prototype can be live in minutes rather than weeks, making it a transformative tool for validating business concepts before investing in a full engineering team.
basic_information.release_date: November 2024 (commercial launch as Lovable; GPT Engineer open-source project launched mid-2023, commercial 'GPT Engineer App' in late 2023)

technical_capabilities.underlying_models: Multi-LLM architecture. Default model is Gemini 3 Flash for speed. Users can prompt the agent to use different models including GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, Gemini 2.5 Pro, or GPT-5 Mini. Historically relied heavily on Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet for complex code generation. Architecture uses a 'hydration' pattern: fast smaller models (e.g., GPT-4 Mini) for initial processing and context selection, then larger models for main code generation.
technical_capabilities.customization_depth: prompt-only for most users (describe what you want in natural language), with a visual editor for direct UI manipulation (color, size, spacing) and a Code Mode on paid plans for direct code editing. GitHub sync enables external code-extension by developers. Supports API integrations and MCP servers for extending functionality.
technical_capabilities.input_types: Text prompts (natural language descriptions), images (for design reference), URLs
technical_capabilities.output_types: Full-stack web applications (React + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS frontend, Supabase/Lovable Cloud backend), deployable apps, code (GitHub export), API endpoints
technical_capabilities.api_access: Yes. Supports REST API integrations within generated apps. MCP server support for personal connectors. No public API for programmatic Lovable project creation (the platform itself is used via its web UI).
technical_capabilities.deployment_options: Cloud-hosted on lovable.app domains (one-click deploy), custom domains on paid plans, GitHub export for self-hosting on Vercel/Netlify/any hosting, Lovable Cloud (managed Supabase backend). Code is standard Vite + React — runs anywhere.
technical_capabilities.ai_model_flexibility: multi-provider. Users can select between multiple AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini) within the platform. The system automatically routes to appropriate models based on task complexity, but users can also manually specify preferred models.

user_experience.target_user: business_user, designer, student, marketer. Primary audience is non-technical founders and entrepreneurs who want to build web apps without coding. Also used by agencies, enterprise IT teams for internal tools, and developers for rapid prototyping.
user_experience.learning_curve: minutes. Users can have a working app skeleton within 5-10 minutes of signing up. The natural language interface requires no technical knowledge to start.
user_experience.setup_time: 5-10 minutes from signup to first working demo app. Creating an account and entering an initial prompt immediately generates a functional application.
user_experience.collaboration_features: Shared workspaces, unlimited collaborators (even on free plan), user roles and permissions (paid plans), GitHub sync for developer collaboration, version history through Git.
user_experience.template_library: Growing library of project templates and starter examples. Design templates available on Business plan. The platform also maintains a video tutorial library and guides showing how to build specific app types (e-commerce, portfolio, SaaS dashboard, etc.).
user_experience.visual_builder_type: hybrid. Combines natural-language prompting (describe what you want) with a Figma-like visual editor (click elements to change color, size, spacing) and optional Code Mode for direct code editing.

ai_and_rag_capabilities.rag_support: Yes, through Supabase/Lovable Cloud integration. Users can connect databases (PostgreSQL via Supabase), upload documents, and build apps that query stored data. Personal connectors (MCP servers) can provide the AI agent with access to internal tools and content during app creation for context-aware building.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.agent_capabilities: multi-step. The Lovable AI agent iterates on code generation across multiple steps: it plans, generates code, previews results, and can self-correct errors. Users refine through conversational prompting. The agent handles frontend, backend, database schema, authentication, and deployment in a coordinated multi-step workflow.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.model_selection: Multi-vendor. Default is Gemini 3 Flash, but users can request GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-5 Mini, or Claude models. The platform manages model routing automatically but allows user override.
ai_and_rag_capabilities.prompt_management: Basic prompt history within projects. No dedicated prompt versioning or optimization features. Users iterate through conversation-style prompting with the AI agent.

integration_and_ecosystem.key_integrations: Supabase (database, auth, storage — native integration), GitHub (automatic code sync), Stripe (payments), Resend (email), Vercel/Netlify (deployment), Google Analytics, custom REST APIs, MCP servers for personal connectors. Lovable Cloud provides managed Supabase infrastructure.
integration_and_ecosystem.integration_count: Not formally counted as a marketplace. Supports three integration types: shared connectors (platform-managed), personal connectors (MCP servers), and any external API. The ecosystem is open-ended rather than connector-counted.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_support: Yes. Lovable supports MCP (Model Context Protocol) for personal connectors, allowing the AI agent to access external tools and content during app creation. There is also a community-built unofficial MCP server (lovable-mcp-server) for analyzing Lovable-generated projects with Claude Desktop.
integration_and_ecosystem.webhook_support: Yes. Lovable-generated apps can receive and send webhooks. External services can push data to Lovable apps via webhook URLs.
integration_and_ecosystem.export_formats: Full source code (React + TypeScript + Vite project) via GitHub sync or manual download. Standard, portable code with no proprietary dependencies. Can be deployed as standalone web applications on any hosting platform. Apps are also deployable directly on lovable.app domains.

pricing_and_accessibility.pricing_model: freemium with credit-based usage. Monthly subscriptions grant credit allocations; each significant AI interaction consumes credits. Student discount available (up to 50% off with university email).
pricing_and_accessibility.free_tier_limits: 5 credits per day (resets every 24 hours), approximately 30 credits per month. Unlimited public projects, unlimited collaborators, GitHub sync, one-click deployment, up to 5 lovable.app domains. Lovable badge displayed on apps. No private projects, no Code Mode, no custom domains.
pricing_and_accessibility.paid_plans: Starter: $25/month — 100 monthly credits (up to 150 with rollover), 5 daily credits, Code Mode, private projects, custom domains, Lovable badge removal, user roles & permissions. Pro (Launch): $50/month — all Starter features plus additional 100 credits (200 total), SSO, personal projects, opt-out of data training, design templates. Teams/Enterprise: $100/month per seat — advanced governance, SSO, SOC2 compliance, dedicated support. Annual billing discounts available.
pricing_and_accessibility.open_source: open-core. The original GPT Engineer project is open-source on GitHub (52,000+ stars, MIT license). The commercial Lovable platform is proprietary SaaS built on top of that foundation. There is also a community open-source boilerplate (lovable-boilerplate) for similar workflows.
pricing_and_accessibility.self_hosting_option: No self-hosting of the Lovable platform itself. However, all generated code can be exported and self-hosted anywhere (standard React/Vite apps). The open-source GPT Engineer can be self-hosted separately.
pricing_and_accessibility.data_residency_and_sovereignty: Company incorporated in Delaware, USA (Lovable Labs Inc.), with engineering team in Stockholm, Sweden. SOC 2 Type 2 compliant, ISO 27001:2022 certified, GDPR compliant. Formal Data Processing Agreement (DPA) available. Data Protection Officer (DPO) appointed. All data encrypted in transit. Opt-out of data training available on Business plan. No explicit EU-only data residency option documented, but GDPR compliance is maintained.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader in the vibe-coding / AI app builder category. Fastest-growing European startup in history. Reached $100M ARR in 8 months, $200M+ ARR by November 2025. $6.6B valuation as of December 2025. Dominant in the non-technical user segment of AI-powered app generation.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Klarna, HubSpot, Photoroom. Used by agencies (e.g., Imaginary Space generating $100k/month building client apps with Lovable). Enterprise customers across 21+ industries, concentrated in Education and Professional Services. Angel investors who are also users include Klarna CEO Sebastian Siemiatkowski, Slack co-founder Stewart Butterfield, HubSpot co-founder Dharmesh Shah.
adoption_and_market.community_size: Nearly 8 million registered users (as of November 2025). 100,000+ new products built on the platform daily. Original GPT Engineer open-source project: 52,000+ GitHub stars. 27,000-person waitlist before commercial launch.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Total funding: ~$530M+. Seed: undisclosed (backed by 20VC, ByFounders, Creandum, Hummingbird, Visionaries Club). Series A (July 2025): $200M at $1.8B valuation, led by Accel. Series B (December 2025): $330M at $6.6B valuation, led by CapitalG and Menlo Ventures, with participation from Khosla Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, Databricks Ventures, NVentures (NVIDIA), Atlassian Ventures, HubSpot Ventures, DST Global, EQT Growth, T. Capital (Deutsche Telekom). Growth: $0 to $200M+ ARR in under 12 months.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Direct competitors: Bolt.new (StackBlitz — browser-based full-stack, WebContainer technology), v0 (Vercel — focused on React UI components), Replit (AI-powered IDE with deployment), Cursor (AI code editor for developers). Adjacent: Bubble (traditional no-code), Webflow (visual web design). Key differentiators: Lovable targets non-technical users with full-stack output (not just UI components like v0), offers seamless Supabase backend integration, and produces standard exportable React code (lower lock-in than Bubble). Bolt competes closest on full-stack, but Lovable's visual editor and managed backend give it an edge for non-coders.
adoption_and_market.ecosystem_lock_in_risk: low. Code is standard React + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind CSS with no proprietary dependencies. Full GitHub export ensures code ownership and portability. Apps can be deployed anywhere. The main lock-in risk is around Lovable Cloud (managed Supabase) and the convenience of the integrated workflow, but the underlying code remains fully portable.

teaching_and_classroom.class_project_idea:
Project 1 — 'Startup Landing Page + Waitlist' (45 min): Students describe their startup idea in 2-3 sentences to Lovable, which generates a professional landing page with email capture form. They iterate on design via the visual editor, connect Supabase for storing signups, and deploy live. Teaches: AI-assisted prototyping, MVP mindset, landing page best practices. Deliverable: a live URL they can share.

Project 2 — 'Mini SaaS Dashboard' (90 min): Students build a simple customer dashboard (e.g., a freelancer invoice tracker or a restaurant order manager) using Lovable + Supabase. They prompt Lovable for the UI, add authentication (Supabase Auth), create a database table, and implement CRUD operations. Teaches: full-stack app architecture, database basics, authentication concepts, and the Build vs Buy decision. Deliverable: a working web app with login, data persistence, and deployment.

teaching_and_classroom.student_prerequisites: nothing. The platform is designed for non-technical users. Basic prompting skills (which M2 students already have as heavy LLM users) are the only prerequisite. Understanding of what a web app does is helpful but not required.
teaching_and_classroom.session_mapping: Session 2 (Prompt engineering & no-code tools): Primary fit — hands-on with AI-powered app building, demonstrates prompt-to-product workflow. Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects): Build vs Buy discussion using Lovable as a case study for rapid prototyping vs custom development. Session 4 (AI business models & strategy): Case study of Lovable's own explosive growth ($0 to $200M ARR in 12 months) and freemium/credit-based business model.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Ideal for: (1) Pre-seed/seed stage startups validating ideas — build a functional MVP in hours instead of weeks, test with real users before hiring engineers. (2) Solo founders and non-technical co-founders who need to demonstrate a working product to investors or early customers. (3) Teams of 1-5 people who want to move fast without dedicated frontend/backend developers. (4) Agencies building client prototypes or MVPs quickly. Less suitable for: complex enterprise applications, apps requiring native mobile performance, or products needing highly customized backend logic beyond what Supabase provides. Best use cases: SaaS dashboards, landing pages with waitlists, internal tools, CRUD applications, marketplaces, and data visualization apps.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_mvp: Minutes to hours for a basic functional MVP. A landing page with email capture can be live in 10-15 minutes. A more complex app with database, auth, and multiple pages can be built in 1-2 days. Lovable claims 20x faster development compared to traditional coding, and real user reports confirm functional apps built and deployed within hours to days rather than weeks.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Use Lovable when: validating an idea quickly (prototype in hours), building internal tools, creating MVPs for fundraising demos, non-technical founder needs a working product fast, budget is limited (<$50/month vs $5,000+/month for a developer). Transition away when: you need complex custom backend logic, native mobile apps, high-performance real-time systems, or your app's complexity exceeds what prompt-driven development can handle efficiently. The low lock-in (standard React code, GitHub export) means you can start with Lovable and hand off to developers later without losing your work — this is a key advantage over proprietary no-code platforms like Bubble.
entrepreneurial_relevance.key_lessons:
1. 'Vibe coding' is real — natural language can now produce production-quality full-stack applications, dramatically lowering the barrier to software entrepreneurship.
2. Start with Lovable for validation, not perfection — use it to test your idea with real users in days, then decide whether to invest in custom engineering.
3. Code ownership matters — unlike traditional no-code (Bubble, Adalo), Lovable exports standard React code you can hand to any developer, avoiding vendor lock-in.
4. The credit system requires budgeting — at $25-50/month, each AI interaction costs credits. Plan your prompts carefully and use the visual editor for small changes instead of burning credits on minor tweaks.
5. Backend integration is the real power — connecting Supabase for database, auth, and storage transforms Lovable from a UI generator into a full product builder. Learn the Supabase integration early.

confidence.data_quality: High. Information sourced from TechCrunch, CNBC, official Lovable documentation, company blog posts, and multiple independent reviews. Funding data confirmed across multiple financial reporting sources.
confidence.cross_reference: TechCrunch (Series A and B coverage), CNBC ($6.6B valuation), Sacra (ARR estimates), official Lovable blog (funding announcements), Contrary Research (business breakdown), multiple independent review sites (BayTech Consulting, Superblocks, eesel.ai), DataCamp and Towards Data Science (technical tutorials).
confidence.caveats: 1. AI model availability evolves rapidly — the specific models available (Gemini 3 Flash, GPT-5.2, etc.) may change as providers release new versions. 2. ARR figures from Sacra ($206M) are estimates; official numbers may differ. 3. The credit-based pricing means actual cost depends heavily on usage patterns — heavy users may find the free/starter tiers insufficient. 4. 'Vibe coding' as a category is very new (term coined by Andrej Karpathy in early 2025) and the competitive landscape is shifting weekly. 5. Lovable is optimized for React/Supabase stack — projects requiring other frameworks or backends will need more manual work after export.
